artists.biography: Solomon Burke (March 21, 1940 – October 10, 2010) was an American recording artist and vocalist, who shaped the sound of rhythm and blues as one of the founding fathers of soul music in the 1960s and a "key transitional figure in the development of soul music from rhythm and blues. He had a string of hits including "Cry to Me", "If You Need Me", "Got to Get You Off My Mind", "Down in the Valley" and "Everybody Needs Somebody to Love". Burke was referred to as "King Solomon", the "King of Rock 'n' Soul", "Bishop of Soul" and the "Muhammad Ali of soul". Due to Burke's minimal chart success in comparison to other soul music greats such as James Brown, Wilson Pickett and Otis Redding, Burke is often described as the genre's "most unfairly overlooked singer" of its golden age.Atlantic Records executive Jerry Wexler once referred to Burke as "the greatest male soul singer of all time".

perplexity.description:
Don't Give Up on Me," released in 2002, is a studio album by Solomon Burke that marked a significant late-career resurgence for the legendary soul and R&B singer. The album is characterized by its blend of funk, soul, and blues, delivered in a raw, organic style recorded live in the studio under the production of Joe Henry. It features a collection of previously unreleased songs written by acclaimed songwriters such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Tom Waits, Elvis Costello, and Dan Penn, among others. These compositions were crafted specifically for Burke, allowing him to reinterpret them with his distinctive, emotive vocal style, reaffirming his influence on multiple generations of musicians.

This album holds a special place in Burke's discography as a comeback that reintroduced him to a broader audience and earned critical acclaim, including the Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Blues Album. The title track, "Don't Give Up on Me," became particularly notable, gaining popularity through its use in the TV show The O.C. and becoming a staple of Burke's live performances. The album's success was both a commercial and artistic triumph, highlighting Burke's enduring relevance and the timeless quality of his voice and interpretive skill. Released originally on Fat Possum Records, the album was later reissued by Anti- Records, further cementing its legacy in Burke's extensive career.
